topic: why 'smart' devices fail more often than the simple tools they replaced
title: Why 'Smart' Devices Break More Than Dumb Ones Did
description: Your old toaster lasted twenty years. Your new smart one might not make it two. Here's why adding chips and wifi to everyday tools quietly makes them less reliable. AI-narrated original commentary.

beats.text: Your grandparents' toaster lasted twenty years. Your smart toaster might not make it two.
beats.broll_query: old toaster next to modern smart appliance

beats.text: Every new 'smart' feature adds a chip, a sensor, a wifi module -- and a new way to fail.
beats.broll_query: circuit board close up with sensors

beats.text: A simple machine has maybe five things that can break. A connected one has fifty.
Manufacturers call it convenience. Repair technicians call it job security.
The single-purpose tools -- the ones that just thresh, just toast, just blend -- rarely need an app to work.
Complexity isn't free. Every added feature hides another point of failure behind a nice interface.
beats.broll_query: smartphone app controlling smart home device

beats.text: That's not an argument against progress -- it's a reminder that 'smart' should mean better, not just more.
Next time a gadget promises to do everything, ask what happens when just one part of it breaks.
